chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Sayyari, who said: A sheikh from our companions narrated to me from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
He said: From the bitterness of the living is moving from one house to another and eating the bread of barley (or coarse bread).
ai.seo_question: What does the Imam consider to be the bitterness of life?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the instability of frequent relocation and the consumption of coarse sustenance as primary markers of life's bitterness, reflecting the socio-economic vulnerabilities of the Shia community during periods of political upheaval. This narration underscores how material precarity serves as a spiritual test, linking physical hardship to the broader Islamic concept of *ghurba* (alienation) and the resilience required of the faithful.
